# Outline — how many benchmarks must be run, which ones, and when does it hold

*Rev. 4, by story-repo (see the revision log). Built from the `Brief` (idea-repo, rev. 5) and the objective (`story-repo`#1). It says what to test and which figure carries which claim; it never says what a result must be. Each claim has a branch for the case it fails — a failing claim is reported as a finding, not repaired.*

## 0. Working title and scope line
"How many benchmarks must you run? Choosing and sizing the run set that predicts a new model's other scores — evidence from embedding-model leaderboards".
The scope line (title/abstract) names the data the claim is about: **MTEB embedding models**, with the realised M × N stated. "LLM"/"language model" appears in the title only if a generative-LLM matrix with N ≳ 20 supports a claim of its own (Gate G2 below). Until then, generative-LLM matrices (Open LLM LB N=6, HELM Lite N=10, LiveBench) are a labelled transfer check restricted to k ≤ N−1.

## 1. The story in six sentences (the abstract's skeleton)
1. Evaluating a model on every benchmark is costly, and leaderboards hold a model × benchmark matrix with holes; an evaluator can afford only k benchmarks for a new model.
2. The problem is cold-start elicitation (new user, k ratings) and multidimensional adaptive testing; the machinery (probabilistic factor model, A/D/V-optimal greedy design) is classical, and we do not claim a new selection method.
3. What is missing for benchmarks is the answer under the protocol that matches the use: whole new models (grouped by org/family) held out, selection and fitting on other models only, error scored on a common target set of benchmarks that no selector can choose (the score on the cells left unrun is kept as a secondary).
4. We give a closed-form risk for the factor model (floor + design term + misfit) and a sufficiency rule k*(ε) tied to the spectrum of the matrix, and we check both on synthetic data (known truth) and on the real matrix.
5. Main result (to be filled by the measurement): the error-vs-k curve on held-out groups, what k reaches ε in raw score points, and whether designed selection beats random-k beyond a pre-set margin — or, if not, that random-k suffices past a small k.
6. Scope map: where the answer holds and where it never reaches the floor (extrapolation to new families/strongest models, sparse coverage, small M, saturation, granularity).

The paper is **evidence-led**: the real-data curve is the headline (Fig. 1), theory explains it, the scope map bounds it. Theory is not the first result on the page, because the data decide whether it is the explanation or only a reference.

## 2. Section plan (what each part says; page split is the venue's call)
| § | Content | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Introduction | evaluator's situation, the question Q, the headline (one sentence with numbers from the final run), contributions list (the three: empirical answer under matching protocol; k*(ε) with misfit term; scope map), explicit "not claimed: new selection algorithm" | Fig. 1 on page 1–2 |
| 2 Related work | the 7 lines in `positioning.md`: in-benchmark item reduction (tinyBenchmarks, metabench, anchor points); low-rank structure of LM scores (observational scaling, Sloth); benchmark agreement (BenchBench); cold-start elicitation; matrix completion/PPCA; subset selection/optimal design; MCAT/IRT. For each: what it does, what it leaves open, what we reuse | positioning |
| 3 Problem and protocol | setting, data matrix definition (one benchmark = one task, rules fixed beforehand), group-wise hold-out, temporal/strength split, **

# Pre-registration of the matrix, split, margin and verdict rules (experiment-repo)

Written by `experiment-repo` in answer to `experiment-repo`#2 (from `idea-repo` Brief rev. 3). The commit that adds this file
(see `git log prereg/PREREG.md`) dates it. **No predictive-error result of any method has been computed when this file is
committed.** What has been looked at: file counts, the number of models/tasks/cells that survive each rule, group sizes and
release-date coverage (structure only). The coverage thresholds R7 were chosen after seeing that count table
(grid of tt in {30..100} x tm in {15..40}); they are not tuned on any score model. Later changes are listed only under
"Deviations" at the end, each with date and reason.

## A. Data (pinned)
`embeddings-benchmark/results` at commit `6dabbcc68c28ea5f180ce7df79347b3ca9cc6383` (2026-03-31), CC0-1.0; 548 model dirs, of which
536 hold task files. Task metadata (type, declared eval splits, modality) from `mteb==2.27.24` via `mteb.get_task(name)` (metadata only).
Scores are `main_score` x 100 ("raw points", 0-100 scale; a few are negative).

## B. Matrix rules (code: `code/mteb_cells.py`, `code/03_build_matrix.py`)
- **R1 one revision per model.** Within a model directory keep the revision directory with the most distinct text-task files; ties -> latest
  `release_date` in its `model_meta.json`, then lexicographically smallest directory name. Revisions are never pooled.
- **R2 benchmark = task.** Only tasks whose mteb modality set is exactly {text}. A benchmark is one task file (task name). Tasks unknown to mteb
  metadata are dropped (12 names, none text).
- **R3 split.** Per (model, task) the first of `test, test.full, validation, validation.full, dev, devtest, default` that is declared in the task's
  `eval_splits` and present. `train` is never used.
- **R4 task version.** A cell is kept only if its `dataset_revision` equals the task's modal `dataset_revision` over models.
- **R5 subsets/languages.** The task's canonical subset set is its modal set of `hf_subset` names over models; a cell is kept iff the model reports a
  superset of it; its score is the mean of `main_score` over the canonical subsets (languages averaged). `mteb_version` of the producing run is
  NOT controlled (stated limitation; sensitivity is a secondary analysis).
- **R6 dedup.** Drop config variants (`_(` in the directory name, e.g. `_(output_dtype=int8)`); of model directories with the same lower-cased
  `model_meta` name keep the one with most cells.
- **R7 coverage filter (iterated to a fixed point).** tasks observed for >= 50 models, models with >= 30 tasks.
- **Group.** org = the part of the directory name before `__`, lower-cased, non-alphanumerics removed, spelling aliases
  `bytedanceseed->bytedance`, `sbert->sentencetransformers` (defined in `mteb_cells.py::ORG_ALIAS`); no other merging (fine-tunes of a third party's
  base model under a different org are NOT merged: limitation, leakage across groups cannot be excluded).
- **Realised shape** (`data/coverage_filter.csv`, `data/matrix_summary.json`): **238 models x 328 tasks, 45,775 cells, density 0.586, 83 org groups**;
  largest group 12 models; run-set size per model min 30, median 221.5; 166 models have >= 109 cells. Task types: Retrieval 117, Classification 73,
  Clustering 56, STS 28, PairClassification 17, Reranking 13, BitextMining 10, MultilabelClassification 8, InstructionReranking 3, Summarization 3.
  Gate G1 (>=100 x >=30, k>=8 possible) is met. 11 of the 238 models have no release date.
